# Workshop programme {.unnumbered}

This book is a comprehensive, self-paced course consisting of 25 teaching units. A selection of 9 units is covered across ten sessions during a 3-day workshop. This page outlines the programme, detailing which units are taught in person and the order in which they are presented.

Each unit in the book, whether taught in the workshop or not, includes a complete chapter, a slide deck, an interactive Pluto notebook, and exercises with solutions. Attending the workshop offers in-person instruction, discussion, and debugging assistance for those 9 units. The remaining 16 units are fully developed and available for self-study, allowing you to work through them at your own pace, whether before, during, or after the workshop.

Each taught session also has a worksheet: a short set of exercises that build on what the session showed, with hints and answer checks. Worksheets live in the `worksheets/` folder of the repository, and worked solutions are added there at the end of each day.

## What the workshop covers

The ten sessions move in the following order: deterministic foundations and discrete time; then stochastic dynamics, model structure, what the data can identify, and how interventions are chosen; then a change of perspective to agent-based models.

- **Day 1: foundations.** A Julia primer, the SIR model derived from first principles, solving ODEs with events, and discrete-time models, deterministic and stochastic.
- **Day 2: beyond the basics.** Continuous-time jump processes, reaction networks and moment closure, sensitivity and identifiability, and interventions and optimisation.
- **Day 3: a new perspective.** Agent-based models across two sessions, building the model and then extending it.

The workshop deliberately stops before parameter estimation and Bayesian inference ([ch12](chapters/12-parameter-estimation.html), [ch13](chapters/13-bayesian-inference.html)). For those interested in fitting models to data and inference, we recommend having a look at the modelling course ["Model Fitting and Inference for Infectious Disease Dynamics"](https://mfiidd.github.io/mfiidd/).

## Before the workshop

Please arrive with Julia, VS Code, and Quarto already installed and the course
packages downloaded. Installing takes far longer than the fifteen-minute
environment check on the first morning.

[**Setting up**](setup.qmd) walks through it step by step, including what to do
when something does not work. Allow about half an hour, most of it waiting for
downloads, and do it on a good connection rather than on workshop wifi.

No prior Julia experience is assumed: Day 1 starts at the REPL. If you would
like to read ahead, [Probability and stochastic
processes](prerequisites/02-probability-and-stochastic-processes.html) and
[Calculus and numerical
methods](prerequisites/03-calculus-and-numerical-methods.html) are useful
background, but they are optional: everything the sessions depend on is
recapped in the session that uses it.
